what: Curtiss-Wright makes engineered products for demanding environments: nuclear reactor components for navy submarines and power stations, aircraft actuation and sensors, and industrial valves and pumps.
customers: The US Navy and defence contractors, nuclear power operators, commercial aircraft manufacturers and industrial customers.
money: embedded computing and electronics for defence platforms
submarine and aircraft carrier components and nuclear plant equipment
moat: Components qualified into navy submarine and nuclear plant programmes, where the approval process takes years and the supplier base is deliberately narrow.
risks: US defence budget decisions drive a large part of revenue
It pays only a small dividend
The shares trade at a high multiple after a strong run
opportunities: Revenue grew about 12% last year and about 11% a year over three years
Analysts see about 38% upside from current levels
Submarine building rates and small modular reactor development both raise demand
watch: Naval and Power orders and the overall backlog.
